title: Retro Over-the-air Weather Channel
blurb: Real time weather over RF airwaves to vintage TVs.
overview: An Open House event at the local Nova Labs makerspace needed exhibits and demos. I had previously been experimenting with local RF signal broadcasting and put together a custom Nova Labs weather channel using the Weatherstar 4000+ open source project.

diary.title: Day 1 — RF Testing
diary.body: Picked up and tested an RF transmitter. Local station channel 11 with NTSC video signal and audio was eventually chosen and configured.

diary.title: Day 2 — Broadcast Sample
diary.body: A laptop and a Playdate handheld game console used the Playdate's Mirror application to view the FMV Game Blippo+ via the RF transmitter to a black and white TV.

diary.title: Day 3 — Raspberry Pi Portable Board
diary.body: A raspberry pi and the RF transmitter and a power strip were mounted to a pegboard so the broadcast system could be easily moved for exhibit displays.

diary.title: Day 4 - Open House
diary.body: The open source project Weatherstar 4000+ was hosted on github pages and the raspberry pi acts as a kiosk to view it. A display at Nova Labs makerspace open house was prepared to broadcast it to multiple vintage TVs over the air.

title: Pizza Time
blurb: Foam and fabric portable pizza oven.
overview: A Halloween event prompted to decorate a vehicle for trick-or-treaters. I decided on a pizza restaurant theme, and needed the back of my vehicle to appear to contain a brick pizza oven. Foam insulation board was used for the faux brick, and the oven flame effect was produced with a laser projector on a bedsheet and a number of portable fans to animate the projection surface. I prepared costumes and props, which allowed for a server and two kitchen chefs to seat and serve children their Halloween candy as though they were at an outdoor restaurant.

diary.title: Concept
diary.body: A rough sketch for the concept. Ensuring the oven opening sizing properly matched a real pizza peel prop which would be used to serve candy to trick-or-treaters. The oven chimney atop the car and pizza themed wheel cover ideas would be cut due to time and complexity constraints.

diary.title: Texture tests
diary.body: Turning foam into brick would need to be convincing. Insulation foam board will deform when a heat gun is applied, and it will have interesting organic patterns when sprayed with water before heat treatment. This approach was interesting, but eventually abandoned, and other avenues would be explored.

diary.title: Paint testing
diary.body: Brick used in building construction and brick used in ovens have distinct differences. Construction brick is often blemished with white-ish mortar or the remnants of removed siding or other adhered materials. Some red brick may be uniform, but layered reds and browns applied with a sponge give an illusion of depth, with shadow and highlights.

diary.title: Brick carving
diary.body: The oven opening, using the size determined previously, and the brick pattern was sharpie'd on. A heated soldering iron was used to carve the brick by melting the foam insulation board which appears organic and non-uniform. A stiff wire brush was used to texture the insulation board for a convincing brick-like appearance.

diary.title: Archway assembly
diary.body: Some insulation board from the removed oven opening was used to cut and shape individual bricks, which would border the opening for additional depth.

diary.title: Painting and portability
diary.body: The brick surface and concrete base were painted using colors from paint testing. A blackened creosete/smoke appearance was added above the oven's opening. The oven was then bisected so it could be transported in the vehicle with passengers and installed within it. This was necessary as the geometry of the rear opening of the vehicle was smaller than the interior cargo area within.

diary.title: Oven flame projector testing
diary.body: The oven would look most impressive in the dark if its interior was animated with glowing flame. This obviously can't be done practically without being dangerous. This video demonstrates how a battery-powered projector with a red light pattern, a bedsheet, and some portable fans were used to simulate the hearth's toasty insides.

diary.title: Day-of setup
diary.body: The installation and props for the pizza kitchen, with various implements for serving candy to trick-or-treaters.

diary.title: Showtime
diary.body: Actors were costumed for interacting with trick-or-treaters, and gave candy and fake moustaches. A wet towel was used to simulate a pizza dough and an actor tossed it about while interacting to animate the scene. Another actor seated the children at the table and took their dinner orders for, what else, but candy.

title: EKG Machine Clue Cabinet
blurb: Animated, aged, abandoned hospital equipment with a secret.
overview: A local escape room was seeking collaboration with local propmakers. After some consultation, I was asked to create a new and engaging container for an existing puzzle clue. The theme for the escape room was a midcentury abandoned hospital. We decided on a piece of abandoned medical machinery. It would encorporate a distressed appearance, a keypad, a magnetic locking, spring-loaded hidden door, an animated display, and some engaging dials, buttons, and knobs.

diary.title: The Escape Room
diary.body: This abandoned wartime hospital room was in need of a unique piece for clue storage behind a keypad lock. The client requested that it accommodate an existing object's dimensions inside, fit beneath the existing wall guard, and accommodate concealed electrical connection to the outlet. It would be bracketed permanently to the wall with a zero-clearance gap, so escape game players would not reach behind it. It would contain a hidden drawer to contain the clue, which should be non-removable to prevent curious gamers from damaging it.

diary.title: Design
diary.body: Initial concept sketches.

diary.title: References
diary.body: 1940s EKG machines were initially paper-fed and needle-marked like a seismograph. Others later used an oscilloscope display which would be both more interesting looking and also more cost effective and reliable to recreate without requiring frequent service. Wooden furniture like a potato storage box had an angled upper portion which could be interesting for a control panel, but a piece of medical equipment like an oscilloscope wasn't the same as a control console. The initial angled display console concept changed to something more like the pictured soviet lab equipment, mixed with the authentic ribbon and paper machine. Highly weathered rust effects would be desired and reference textures were recorded.

diary.title: CNC Parts
diary.body: The ShopSabre CNC router machine would be used to create precision cuts for multiple materials and overlays for the face of the device. The acrylic lens, the bezels of the front panel, and the voids on the front and the back would be routed in with this process.
